title: Pointwise basic-open detection from the fraction formula
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], L an invertible module [def-sc-invertible-module], S its graded section ring [def-sc-invertible-section-ring], and f:X -> Proj(S) [def-pc-proj]. Assume that for each homogeneous s of positive degree d, every n >= 0 and every homogeneous xi of degree nd, on f^{-1}(D_+(s)) one has f^sharp(xi/s^n) s^n = xi, as an identity of restricted tensor-power sections. Let x in X admit a positive-degree homogeneous section t which is nonvanishing at x [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. For every homogeneous s of positive degree, f(x) lies in D_+(s) if and only if s is nonvanishing at x. Only the point x is required to lie outside the base locus.

source.place: Constructions Lemma 01N8 (lemma-converse-construction), local quotient construction, overlap and inverse-image calculation; Properties Lemma 01PZ (lemma-map-into-proj), proof and clause (1)

proof.text: Trivialize L near x and pass to the residue field. A section of each tensor power is a scalar times the corresponding tensor power of a basis. Tensor product, ring multiplication and positive powers of sections become scalar product and positive powers, so positive powers preserve both vanishing and nonvanishing. This also respects the tensor-power addition isomorphisms used in the section ring.

source.place: Constructions Lemma 01N8 (lemma-converse-construction), local quotient construction, overlap and inverse-image calculation; Properties Lemma 01PZ (lemma-map-into-proj), proof and clause (1)

proof.text: Suppose f(x) belongs to D_+(s), with degree d. Choose t as in the pointwise hypothesis, with positive degree e. Apply the fraction identity with denominator s^e and numerator t^d. In the fibre the right side is nonzero. Thus s^e, and therefore s, is nonzero.

source.place: Constructions Lemma 01N8 (lemma-converse-construction), local quotient construction, overlap and inverse-image calculation; Properties Lemma 01PZ (lemma-map-into-proj), proof and clause (1)

proof.text: Conversely, suppose s is nonvanishing at x. Choose a positive-degree homogeneous t with f(x) in D_+(t), using the standard affine cover of Proj; write e for its degree. The identity for s^e/t^d first forces t^d to have nonzero fibre at x. Since both s^e and t^d are nonzero, the pullback of the chart function s^e/t^d has nonzero residue at x. Locality of the stalk homomorphism of f reflects units, so this chart function is a unit at f(x). On the chart D_+(t) its unit locus is D_+(s) intersect D_+(t); hence f(x) is in D_+(s). This establishes the reverse implication without a global covering hypothesis.

The fraction pullback identity for a morphism into Proj implies that a point is in the inverse image of a homogeneous basic open exactly when the corresponding invertible module section does not vanish
